transcript.text: Before we jump in, anything that came up internally since last time that you want to make sure we cover?
Actually, yeah. One thing I want to clear up.

So it came up on our side. One of the folks on my team said, and honestly the Datadog rep kind of said the same thing when we talked to them, that Arize is really more for traditional ML. Like tabular models, drift, that world. Not really built for LLM apps. And we're, like, ninety percent LLM stuff now. Claims intake, the adjuster copilot, all of it.
So is that, is that wrong? I'm genuinely asking, I don't know.

knowledge.title: Product scope: LLM and agent applications
knowledge.text: Arize supports LLM and agent applications (tracing, evaluations including LLM-as-a-judge, code-based checks and human annotation, prompt iteration and production monitoring) alongside traditional ML observability.

knowledge.title: Competitive positioning: general guidance
knowledge.text: Anchor on the buyer's own evaluation criteria first. Arize talking points: OpenTelemetry-based tracing via OpenInference instrumentation; open-source Phoenix for local development and experimentation; tracing, evaluation and production monitoring in one workflow; enterprise deployment options. Do not make specific claims about a named competitor's features, roadmap or pricing; ask what the buyer has seen.

Attacks Datadog, the Datadog rep or Nadia's teammate
Overstates capabilities beyond the approved source (invented feature names, customer counts, benchmarks)
Makes claims about Datadog's own products
Treats the buyer's genuine question as an objection she holds
